body.name: Exact-dyadic directed-rounding model \(\mathbb F_n^{\mathrm{dir}}\)
body.construction: The deterministic input consists of exact signed dyadic arrays \(\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C\), exact dyadic public controls \(\alpha,\sigma,c,C_0,B\), and exact integer controls, each with total numerator, exponent, and control-description bit length at most \(L_n\).  Computation uses MPFR-equivalent radix-two arithmetic with a \(q_n\)-bit normalized significand, correctly rounded operations in both round-toward-minus-infinity and round-toward-plus-infinity modes, and an arbitrary-precision signed exponent.  Overflow and subnormal values therefore do not occur in this abstract model.  An IEEE 754 backend must instead apply certified exact power-of-two rescaling, widen its exponent range before endpoint emission whenever an overflow or subnormal flag is possible, and reject every flushed value.  Bit cost counts \(n,L_n,p_n,q_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\) and the bit lengths of all dynamically stored exponents.  A corollary using a refinable non-dyadic public control is outside this input model unless it supplies a known uniform time-and-output-size modulus, incorporates that modulus into \(L_n\), and records the returned control interval as input uncertainty.
